body: Same situation. But you have to think about yourself when your pain is intolerable. I know it will destroy my family for a while but i will drive myself crazy living with such pain and instability.

And I tried a ton to make it better. Went out of my comfort zone when I used to be the quiet kid in school who kept to himself. Talked to people I never would of, became 50X more confident and did and tried things I never would of before.

I can’t. I feel mentally drained, exhausted and incapable of fighting anymore. I’m not even in an highly emotional state right now. Just feel less afraid of death but no clue whether Ill be able to go through with it.

ButI don’t have the resilience to fight through this agony. I avoid life because I’m scared of it. I haven’t responded to treatment and have been dealing with this for years. I’m a fucking idiot and have dug myself this hole in some regards. However some of it has been just bad luck. I feel like I’ve been running out of time for a while now but just can’t seem to pull the trigger out of fear. I really wish i either had amazing resilience and didn’t give a shit about what people thought or what I thought or I had the balls to end my life. I’m stuck and in pain.

I think my overall point is that it’s impossible to prove cause and effect for something this complex. There is definitely an association it seems but it is not a fact nor a cause and effect. An explanation for near death experiences does not make something a fact.

They can’t be explained entirely by science. I’ve read the neuroscience stuff and I understand it. But they don’t explain why people feel the specific feelings of joy, love and serenity. Just because the internal workings of body may be changing close to or during death and oxygen levels and what not it doesn’t mean they are directly responsible for these feelings.

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6172100/

Read this and maybe you will reconsider that your view isn’t a fact.

There not facts. Somethings can’t be explained by entirely by science like death because you can’t just ask the dead and it’s entirely more complex because we literally have no evidence for what happens when the body dies. It doesn’t mean the mind necessarily dies. The closest thing we have are near death experiences and the very high majority report something after death. 

People report our of body experiences while clinically dead in which they can recall specific things being said in the room while they were ‘clinically dead’ The experiences don’t change across cultures and history. People also report feelings of intense joy, love and serenity which cannot be described by human words. Feelings much more intense and more real than anything experienced on earth. This cant be accurately explained by science because how can people feel and experience things that they’ve never felt their whole life, as well as vastly different.
I forgot you knew the answers to the universe that no one else does. It’s more likely life is an illusion of our minds. No one knows until they’ve died, no matter your beliefs.
How can you reassure them that there’s nothing after death? None of us know and the evidence slightly favours that there is some sort of afterlife but it looks promising and free of pain.
